theme.title: Going to work
theme.subtitle: Detroit Pistons, 2003–04
theme.recap: Detroit's defense-first underdogs rallied after a midseason trade and toppled a star-studded Lakers team for the title.

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did the 2003–04 Pistons win?
questions.note: 54–28, before the defense-first Pistons won the title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: finishing second in the Central Division with a 54–28 record

funFacts.text: Detroit used its 2003 second-overall draft pick on Darko Miličić, who played a limited reserve role during the title season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They selected Darko Miličić as their top pick but only used him as a reserve

funFacts.text: Larry Brown arrived as head coach after Detroit reached the Eastern Conference finals the year before.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: After their first trip to the Conference Finals since 1991, the Pistons hired Larry Brown as head coach.

funFacts.text: The Pistons clinched the title at their home arena, the Palace of Auburn Hills, outside downtown Detroit.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Palace of Auburn Hills, Auburn Hills, Michigan

questions.prompt: How many straight games did Larry Brown's Pistons win across December and January?
questions.note: Thirteen straight during Brown's first season in Detroit.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they went on a 13-game winning streak between December and January

funFacts.text: That midwinter streak was part of Larry Brown's first year running Detroit, after he replaced the previous coaching staff.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: After their first trip to the Conference Finals since 1991, the Pistons hired Larry Brown as head coach.

funFacts.text: The championship season wasn't all smooth: Detroit also suffered a six-game losing streak in February.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they struggled in February, losing six straight games.

funFacts.text: Detroit finished second in its own Central Division yet still went on to win the league championship.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: finishing second in the Central Division with a 54–28 record.

questions.prompt: After trading for Rasheed Wallace, how many of its final 19 games did Detroit win?
questions.note: Sixteen wins in the final 19 games helped lock in Detroit's playoff form.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: With the addition of Wallace, the Pistons won 16 of their final 19 games

funFacts.text: Rasheed had played just one game for Atlanta before being moved to Detroit in the middle of the season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the team acquired All-Star forward Rasheed Wallace from the Atlanta Hawks after playing just one game for them.

funFacts.text: The Pistons had to recover from a dangerous deficit against New Jersey in Game 6 to stay alive in the Eastern playoffs.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Pistons were able to erase a 13–2 deficit and never trailed for the remainder of the game

funFacts.text: Detroit reached the Finals by eliminating the top-seeded Pacers in a defensive Eastern Conference finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they defeated the top-seeded Indiana Pacers in a defensive six game series

questions.prompt: What did 2004 Finals MVP Chauncey Billups average in points per game?
questions.context: Detroit Pistons vs Lakers · 2004 Finals · five games
questions.note: 21.0 per game for the Finals MVP, on 50.9% shooting.

funFacts.text: Billups shot better than 50% from the field and over 47% from three during the championship series.
The Lakers entered the matchup favored, with a lineup led by Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O'Neal.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Lakers, headed by Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O'Neal, were considered the heavy favorites

funFacts.text: Richard Hamilton actually averaged slightly more points than Billups in that series, despite Billups taking Finals MVP.

questions.prompt: How many rebounds did Ben Wallace grab in Game 5 of the 2004 Finals?
questions.context: Detroit Pistons vs Lakers · June 15, 2004 · championship clincher
questions.note: Twenty-two rebounds in the win that sealed the title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Rebs: Ben Wallace 22

funFacts.text: Detroit's title-clinching win was the only game of that Finals in which either team reached triple digits.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Pistons' 100 points was the first (and only) time either team scored triple digits in the series.

funFacts.text: Karl Malone was unable to dress for the decisive Game 5 because of a knee injury, ending his last NBA Finals run.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Karl Malone would play his last game, as a knee injury would not allow him to dress in Game 5.

funFacts.text: Detroit owner William Davidson had celebrated another title just days earlier: his Tampa Bay Lightning won the Stanley Cup.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Pistons' owner William Davidson became the first owner in American sports history to win two championships in one calendar year;
